summary: event-emitter-testmetest ships an encrypted self-decrypting payload eval'd on require
details: The package advertises an event-emitter utility but ships no event-emitter code. The sole file index.js is a single IIFE that executes at require time: a numeric char-code array is converted to text, a Caesar shift (k=19) recovers inner JavaScript source, and that source imports node:crypto, AES-128-GCM-decrypts a large embedded hex ciphertext using a hardcoded key/IV/authTag, and passes the decrypted bytes to eval. The decrypted code is not inspectable without executing it. Any consumer that imports this package runs attacker-chosen code on the installer's machine with no network fetch required — the hostile payload is embedded in the tarball itself behind two layers of obfuscation (Caesar wrapper around AES-GCM ciphertext).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
